PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)

comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```

ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4

settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)

comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)

comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)

comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)

comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Before applying `plot_settings` 
```

ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))

```

settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))

plt.show()

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

```

ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))

plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

The change adds a link to the latest VSO Health Report, which provides up-to-date status on VSO data retrieval. 

### Changes
The output of the Fido results now includes the followinf string: 
`Latest VSO data retrieval status available at https://docs.virtualsolar.org/wiki/VSOHealthReport`
This will provide users with a direct link to the VSO Health Report for more status on the data  retrieval

### Example Output:
```
Results from 1 Provider:

Source: http://vso.stanford.edu/cgi-bin/search

2012-03-04 00:00:00.000 2012-03-04 00:00:01.000    SDO        AIA 171.0 .. 171.0     JSOC intensity   NARROW         4096          4096    FULLDISK 64.64844

Latest VSO data retrieval status available at https://docs.virtualsolar.org/wiki/VSOHealthReport
```
Feel free to leave any feedback or suggestions on this change. Thanks

The change adds a link to the latest VSO Health Report, which provides up-to-date status on VSO data retrieval.

The output of the Fido results now includes the followinf string: 
`Latest VSO data retrieval status available at https://docs.virtualsolar.org/wiki/VSOHealthReport`
This will provide users with a direct link to the VSO Health Report for more status on the data  retrieval

Latest VSO data retrieval status available at https://docs.virtualsolar.org/wiki/VSOHealthReport
```
Feel free to leave any feedback or suggestions on this change. Thanks

pull request introduces an update to the output of the Fido results when using the VSOClient. The change adds a link to the latest VSO Health Report, which provides up-to-date status on VSO data retrieval. 

### Changes
The output of the Fido results now includes the followinf string: 
`Latest VSO data retrieval status available at https://docs.virtualsolar.org/wiki/VSOHealthReport`
This will provide users with a direct link to the VSO Health Report for more status on the data  retrieval

### Example Output:
```
Results from 1 Provider:

1 Results from the VSOClient:
Source: http://vso.stanford.edu/cgi-bin/search
Total estimated size: 67.789 Mbyte

                                                                     Angstrom                                                                        Mibyte 
----------------------- ----------------------- ------ ---------- -------------- -------- --------- -------- ------------ ------------- ----------- --------
2012-03-04 00:00:00.000 2012-03-04 00:00:01.000    SDO        AIA 171.0 .. 171.0     JSOC intensity   NARROW         4096          4096    FULLDISK 64.64844

Latest VSO data retrieval status available at https://docs.virtualsolar.org/wiki/VSOHealthReport
```
Feel free to leave any feedback or suggestions on this change. Thanks

pull request introduces an update to the output of the Fido results when using the VSOClient. The change adds a link to the latest VSO Health Report, which provides up-to-date status on VSO data retrieval. 

### Changes
The output of the Fido results now includes the followinf string: 
`Latest VSO data retrieval status available at https://docs.virtualsolar.org/wiki/VSOHealthReport`
This will provide users with a direct link to the VSO Health Report for more status on the data  retrieval

### Example Output:
```
Results from 1 Provider:

1 Results from the VSOClient:
Source: http://vso.stanford.edu/cgi-bin/search
Total estimated size: 67.789 Mbyte

       Start Time               End Time        Source Instrument   Wavelength   Provider  Physobs  Wavetype Extent Width Extent Length Extent Type   Size  
                                                                     Angstrom                                                                        Mibyte 
----------------------- ----------------------- ------ ---------- -------------- -------- --------- -------- ------------ ------------- ----------- --------
2012-03-04 00:00:00.000 2012-03-04 00:00:01.000    SDO        AIA 171.0 .. 171.0     JSOC intensity   NARROW         4096          4096    FULLDISK 64.64844

Latest VSO data retrieval status available at https://docs.virtualsolar.org/wiki/VSOHealthReport
```
Feel free to leave any feedback or suggestions on this change. Thanks

pull request introduces an update to the output of the Fido results when using the VSOClient. The change adds a link to the latest VSO Health Report, which provides up-to-date status on VSO data retrieval. 

### Changes
The output of the Fido results now includes the followinf string: 
`Latest VSO data retrieval status available at https://docs.virtualsolar.org/wiki/VSOHealthReport`
This will provide users with a direct link to the VSO Health Report for more status on the data  retrieval

### Example Output:
```
Results from 1 Provider:

1 Results from the VSOClient:
Source: http://vso.stanford.edu/cgi-bin/search
Total estimated size: 67.789 Mbyte

       Start Time               End Time        Source Instrument   Wavelength   Provider  Physobs  Wavetype Extent Width Extent Length Extent Type   Size  
                                                                     Angstrom                                                                        Mibyte 
----------------------- ----------------------- ------ ---------- -------------- -------- --------- -------- ------------ ------------- ----------- --------
2012-03-04 00:00:00.000 2012-03-04 00:00:01.000    SDO        AIA 171.0 .. 171.0     JSOC intensity   NARROW         4096          4096    FULLDISK 64.64844

Latest VSO data retrieval status available at https://docs.virtualsolar.org/wiki/VSOHealthReport
```
Feel free to leave any feedback or suggestions on this change. Thanks

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4

settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

+        This method modifies the input dictionary `contour_args` to reflect the

+
+        Parameters
+        ----------
+        contour_args : dict
+            A dictionary of arguments to be used for contour plotting.
+
+        Returns
+        -------

+        - 'origin': If `'origin': 'lower'` is present, it is replaced with `'origin': None`,
+        as `None` is the default value for Matplotlib's contour plots.
+        """

+        contour_args.update(plot_settings)

+        }

+        }

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

+        Parameters
+        ----------
+        contour_args : dict
+            A dictionary of arguments to be used for contour plotting.

+        Returns

+        - 'origin': If `'origin': 'lower'` is present, it is replaced with `'origin': None`,
+        as `None` is the default value for Matplotlib's contour plots.

```
Feel free to leave any feedback or suggestions on this change. Thanks

The output of the Fido results now includes the followinf string: 
`Latest VSO data retrieval status available at https://docs.virtualsolar.org/wiki/VSOHealthReport`
This will provide users with a direct link to the VSO Health Report for more status on the data  retrieval

### Example Output:
```
Results from 1 Provider:

1 Results from the VSOClient:
Source: http://vso.stanford.edu/cgi-bin/search

----------------------- ----------------------- ------ ---------- -------------- -------- --------- -------- ------------ ------------- ----------- --------
2012-03-04 00:00:00.000 2012-03-04 00:00:01.000    SDO        AIA 171.0 .. 171.0     JSOC intensity   NARROW         4096          4096    FULLDISK 64.64844

Latest VSO data retrieval status available at https://docs.virtualsolar.org/wiki/VSOHealthReport
```
Feel free to leave any feedback or suggestions on this change. Thanks

### Related Issue:
- Resolves #7853

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

Describe the feature

More information about VSO data acquisition status.

### Proposed solution

The VSO has a "health report" page here: https://docs.virtualsolar.org/wiki/VSOHealthReport . It would be useful for the user to be able to have a link to this health report when Fido results that use `VSOClient` are shown. This would look something like what is the typical output shown in https://docs.sunpy.org/en/stable/tutorial/acquiring_data/index.html . I have added in an extra line:

```
import astropy.units as u

Fido.search(a.Time('2012/3/4', '2012/3/4'), a.Instrument.aia,
            a.Wavelength(171*u.angstrom))  
<sunpy.net.fido_factory.UnifiedResponse object at ...>
Results from 1 Provider:

Latest VSO data retrieval status available at https://docs.virtualsolar.org/wiki/VSOHealthReport
1 Results from the VSOClient:
```

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)

```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

```

ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
